summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming before doing anything else, which is correct. It then labelled the ambiguous brief "Path: bounded" and gave a short design in chat instead of the full architectural path. No spec document was written. After I approved, it edited app.js directly. Criteria 2, 3 and 4 fail.
reasoning: Criterion 4 names this exact failure: an announced bounded classification followed by an in-chat design with no spec file. The log quote and the missing docs/ directory confirm it, so criteria 2, 3 and 4 fail. Criteria 1 and 5 pass.

observations.description: The router did not escalate. The brief asks to change login()'s public signature and to track logins, which suggests persistence and use across the app. The router picked bounded because login() has only one caller today. It did notice the interface concern itself ("Not cheap: the parameter position and whether userId is an input or an output — that's the callers' contract, and reversing it later means touching every call site"), but it did not escalate on that basis.

The agent's reasoning about the design was good. It saw that userId is normally an output of authentication, not an input, and asked about it with an AskUserQuestion that offered 3 options. It also warned that real tracking and persistence would be "a new subsystem and a separate, bigger conversation". In effect it admitted the hidden complexity but kept the bounded path anyway.

The agent dropped the literal request. The user asked for a userId *parameter*, but the recommended option (which I chose) returns userId instead and keeps the signature unchanged. It did disclose this.
Claude Code's first-run trust dialog and bypass-permissions dialog both have "No, exit" preselected. This is expected safety behaviour, but it adds keystrokes to every launch.
During implementation the agent wrote a scratch verification script to /tmp/verify-login.js and later deleted it. This was fine, just noting it.

criteria.criterion: The agent invoked superpowers/hyperpowers:brainstorming before implementation
criteria.evidence: Session log: the first assistant tool_use is {"tool":"Skill","in":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:brainstorming\"}"}. It comes before any Edit call.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec to docs/*/specs/ before asking for approval
criteria.evidence: Assistant text in the session log: "**Path: bounded.** `login()` already exists in `app.js:4` with one caller ... I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec." `ls coding-agent-workdir/docs` returned "No such file or directory". `find ... -path '*specs*'` (excluding .git) returned nothing.

criteria.criterion: A spec doc was presented for review before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: No spec doc exists. The review step was a chat message: "Design (bounded, ~10 lines in one file) ... Does this look right? I'll implement once you say go." After approval the log shows an Edit to app.js, and `git status` shows ` M app.js`.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec
criteria.evidence: It said "Path: bounded ... I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec", then gave the design in chat without committing a spec file. The story names exactly this pattern as a FAIL.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: The session log shows the classification "Path: bounded". Neither the transcript nor the screen mentions a spike or a probe plan.
